summary: This note describes the 2018 NBA draft, held June 21, 2018, at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York, and televised nationally by ESPN. It covers the final use of the original weighted lottery system, which was agreed in 2017 but scheduled to be replaced from the 2019 draft, and the NCAA's August 8, 2018 decision letting undrafted underclassmen return to school. The note also reports that the Phoenix Suns won the first overall pick, selecting Bahamian center Deandre Ayton from the University of Arizona. The text mixes past-tense and future-tense wording for the same events, apparently from different versions of the article.
one_line: Summary of the 2018 NBA draft held June 21, 2018 in Brooklyn, won first overall by the Phoenix Suns, who took Deandre Ayton.
key_facts: The 2018 NBA draft was held on June 21, 2018, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York.
The draft was televised nationally by ESPN.
The 2018 draft was the last to use the original weighted lottery system, which gave teams near the bottom of the draft better odds at the top three picks.
The weighted lottery rule was agreed upon by the NBA on September 28, 2017, but would not be implemented until the 2019 draft.
On August 8, 2018, the NCAA announced that players who declared for the NBA draft and were not selected could return to their school for at least another year.
The Phoenix Suns won the first overall pick in the draft lottery on May 15, 2018.
The NBA draft lottery was held in Chicago instead of in New York.
The Sacramento Kings received the second overall pick and the Atlanta Hawks received the third overall pick.
The Suns' selection was their first No. 1 overall selection in franchise history.
The Phoenix Suns used the first overall pick on Bahamian center Deandre Ayton from the University of Arizona.
The draft was the final year in which undrafted college underclassmen were forced to begin their professional careers early, according to the note.
